title: Last Light
summary: At sunset in a high-rise bar Rogue keeps for herself, V picks the cheapest of three glasses and tells one small true story.
description: Rogue has a bar for the evening, a high-rise in City Center Downtown, and she will buy. She asks V to come at sunset and tell one small true story.

start.bringUp: You want V at a high-rise bar in City Center Downtown at sunset, where you will buy and V tells a story. Bring up, briefly and in your own way, that you have a bar for the evening and want company.

variations.know: Rain runs down the glass as the sun goes, and the skyline is grey.
It is a late-night bar, and the sunset has already gone.
The bartender pours a single-malt flight instead of three glasses.

bar.name: the high-rise bar in City Center Downtown

bar-rain.name: the high-rise bar in the rain

bar-late.name: the high-rise bar late at night

bar-flight.name: the high-rise bar with a single-malt flight

g1.asks: Your turn. Something true and small. Not a war story.
g1.know: The bartender has poured three glasses at sunset, and the second is the cheapest. Rogue has just told a small story, and V's story should be brief. The sun is going down behind the skyline.
g1.secret: That she has not told a small story in years.

stages.label: V picks the cheapest of three glasses at sunset
stages.objective: Pick the cheapest of three glasses with Rogue at the high-rise bar
stages.know: You are at the bar at sunset with V. The bartender pours three glasses. You buy, and you want V to pick the cheapest glass by tag. You will then tell a short story and ask V for one.
stages.wants: V to pick the cheapest of the three glasses, and then tell a small true story.

do.who: bartender who knew Rogue in the old days, who tells one harmless story about her

choices.means: V picks the first or the third glass

right-glass.memory: You picked the cheapest of the three glasses at sunset, and Rogue let the bartender tell her story.

wrong-glass.memory: You picked a dearer glass at sunset, and Rogue let it go.

declined.memory: You would not pick a glass at sunset, and the bartender poured one for you anyway.
